title: Functional and Anatomical Outcomes of Pars Plana Vitrectomy for Lamellar Macular Hole: Long-Term Follow-Up
condition: Symptomatic lamellar macular hole (OCT consensus criteria), all eyes phakic, no previous intraocular surgery; 16 eyes of 14 patients operated 2015-2020 at Careggi University Hospital, Florence; interventional study built from reviewed records (16 of 36 reviewed eyes met the inclusion criteria, which required OCT at 1 and 6 months and at least 36 months of follow-up)

groups.agent: 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy with epiretinal proliferation and ILM peeling (trypan blue/Blulife staining), SF6 20% gas tamponade, combined with cataract surgery and IOL implantation in all eyes
groups.description: Whole cohort, one operation per eye; face-down positioning 3-5 days

exclusions.reason: Undated final visit (follow-up ranged 36-74 months after surgery); undated final-visit columns are excluded
Duplicate of the Table 3 preoperative value for the same eyes; Table 3 cited

notes: Treatment vitrectomy; cataract surgery with IOL was combined with vitrectomy in every eye (co-intervention, same arm).
Measure: CFT determined by automated OCT software measurement without definition of the subfield: central_unspecified.
Device other: preoperative and postoperative scans came from Nidek RS-3000, Heidelberg Spectralis or Optovue RTVue (mixed devices); the long-term examination used Spectralis.
Role control: standard surgery, single cohort without an investigational arm.

series.notes: Mean (SD) per Table 3 footnote; times from surgery (1 and 6 months); Methods state no patient was lost to follow-up (n = 16 at every visit); comparisons used linear mixed models but the tabulated values are observed means
